narrationScript: This holographic chart visualizes Big O growth rates. O(1), the flat blue line, shows constant time, independent of input 'n'. O(log n), the green line, is highly efficient, growing very slowly as problems are repeatedly halved. O(n), the yellow line, represents linear growth: double input, double time. Crucially, the red line, O(n^2), shows quadratic time. It shoots up dramatically! Doubling the input quadruples the time. While differences are minor for small 'n', for large datasets, the performance gap between O(n) and O(n^2) becomes immense. This visual underscores that choosing an algorithm with a lower growth rate is fundamental for building performant and scalable software.
deliveryNotes: Point out each line on the chart
Emphasize the dramatic increase of O(n^2)
